bib.title: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs", Xingyu Chen, Jiahao Xu, Tian Liang, Zhiwei He et al. (Tencent AI Lab, SJTU), arXiv:2412.21187v2 [cs.CL], 1 Feb 2025. Preprint.

COVERAGE: the full extraction, 52,193 chars, 17 pages. The body (pp.1-12), references (skimmed) and appendix (A.1 Figure 8 case, A.2 clustering prompt) were all read. Figure data came through as number soup; I read table values only from the tables. There is no limitations section.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: o1-like models spend far more tokens than conventional models on trivial questions.
  number: 1,953% more tokens on "2 plus 3"
  setup: Figure 1(a) compares o1-like models with conventional LLMs on one question. The abstract text names QwQ-32B-Preview and DeepSeek-R1. The 13-solution example in Fig. 2 is QwQ.
  quote: "On average, o1-like models consumed 1,953% more tokens than conventional models to reach the same answer."
  where: p.2, §1
- Claim: in almost every case the first solution is already correct, so later solutions rarely add accuracy.
  number: >92% (per-set values 89-97% in Fig. 5)
  setup: QwQ-32B-Preview and DeepSeek-R1 on ASDIV and MATH500. Only responses with a correct answer are counted.
  quote: "In more than 92% of cases, the initial round of solutions produces the correct answer. Notably, the first round generally comprises less than 60% of the total tokens generated"
  where: p.5, §2.2
- Claim: the first solution is a minority of the tokens spent.
  number: 287 tokens, 38.7% of the response
  setup: QwQ-32B-Preview on ASDIV.
  quote: "the average length of the first round of solutions for QwQ-32B-Preview on the ASDIV test set is 287 tokens, constituting only 38.7% of the entire response"
  where: p.5
- Claim: models produce more solution rounds on easier problems even though tokens rise with difficulty.
  number: QwQ 3.7 rounds (levels 1-2) vs 3.0 (levels 4-5); R1 4.6 vs 3.9. Mean solutions on ASDIV vs MATH500: QwQ 3.5 vs 3.2, R1 4.5 vs 4.3.
  setup: MATH500 difficulty levels 1-5, QwQ-32B-Preview and DeepSeek-R1. Solutions are split by Llama-3.3-70B.
  quote: "generate more solution rounds for problems at easier levels 1-2 (e.g., averaging 3.7 rounds and 4.6 rounds, respectively) compared to levels 4-5 (e.g., averaging 3.0 rounds and 3.9 rounds, respectively), despite the number of tokens consistently increasing with the difficulty level."
  where: p.4, §2.1
- Claim: most responses contain 2-4 solution rounds.
  number: 76-80% for QwQ, 59-63% for R1
  setup: ASDIV, GSM8K and MATH500.
  quote: "o1-like models produce 2 to 4 solution rounds for most instances, covering 76% to 80% of cases for QwQ-32B-Preview across the test sets and 59% to 63% for DeepSeek-R1."
  where: p.3
- Claim: later solutions repeat earlier strategies, and the second solution is usually a same-strategy double-check.
  number: the distinctness ratio for solution #≥4 is 11.5% lower than for #3. Fig. 6 values for solution #2 are 24-34%, #3 is 29-47%.
  setup: GPT-4o clusters solutions by reasoning strategy. ASDIV and MATH500, QwQ and R1.
  quote: "the average distinctness ratio for Solution#≥4 across test sets decreases by 11.5% compared to Solution#3."
  where: p.6
- Claim: efficiency table. The o1-like models match or beat conventional models on accuracy but use 2-5x the tokens and score 42-52% on outcome efficiency.
  number: ASDIV QwQ 96.9% acc / 741.8 tokens / 41.9% outcome / 66.5% process, vs Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct 95.6% / 166.4 tokens. MATH500 QwQ 93.0 / 2407.9 tokens / 52.3% / 71.2%, vs Qwen2.5-Math-72B 86.8 / 593.1 tokens. R1 on MATH500: 96.4 / 2704.3 tokens / 51.0% / 66.2%.
  setup: Table 1. Outcome efficiency ξO = mean over instances of σᵢ·T̂ᵢ/Tᵢ. Process efficiency ξP = mean of Dᵢ/Tᵢ.
  quote: "QwQ-32B-Preview 93.0 3.2 2407.9 52.3% 71.2%"
  where: p.7, Table 1
- Claim: overthinking is worst on the easiest problems, and the easiest tier gets worse outcome efficiency.
  number: ASDIV outcome efficiency is lower than the harder sets' (47.9% at ASDIV level 1 in the extraction). MATH500 level 1 is 57.5% (QwQ) and 57.1% (R1), falling to 46.4% and 42.4% at level 5.
  setup: Fig. 7. The extraction of the figure is garbled, so the pairing of efficiency curves to labels is uncertain.
  quote: "These findings underscore that the overthinking issues faced by o1-like models are particularly pronounced with simpler math problems."
  where: p.7. Caution: the text says "less than 50% outcome efficiency" for level 1, which does not match the MATH500 level-1 figure above. Check Fig. 7 before citing a level-wise number.
- Claim: the paper's fix is self-training with SimPO on FCS+Reflection data. It cuts tokens roughly in half on MATH500 with accuracy within about 0.2 points.
  number: MATH500 QwQ 93.0 / 2407.9 tokens becomes 92.8 / 1330.7 tokens (outcome 80.0%, process 89.5%). Fig. 1 states a 48.6% token reduction on MATH500.
  setup: QwQ-32B-Preview, PRM12K training prompts, 10 samples each at temperature 1.0, wrong samples discarded, shortest sample of each type kept. SimPO was best of SFT, DPO, RPO and SimPO. The negative example is the longest sample.
  quote: "our approach can reduce token output by 48.6% while maintaining accuracy on the widely-used MATH500 testset as applied to QwQ-32B-Preview."
  where: p.2 and Table 4, p.10
- Claim: keeping only the first correct solution is most efficient but hurts accuracy on hard problems.
  number: MATH500: FCS 91.0 / 1016.0 tokens / 88.7% outcome; FCS+Reflection 92.8 / 1330.7; GDS 91.8 / 1286.1; baseline 93.0.
  setup: Table 4, QwQ-32B-Preview + SimPO.
  quote: "this method decreases performance on the difficult MATH500 test set, which may require more rounds of reflection."
  where: p.10
- Claim: on easy sets the method keeps or improves accuracy while halving tokens. On hard sets accuracy holds within a few points but dips.
  number: ASDIV 96.9 to 96.8, tokens 741.8 to 381.6. GSM8K 94.8 to 96.0, tokens 772.8 to 416.6. GPQA 59.6 to 59.1, tokens 3228.4 to 2085.7. AIME24 46.7 to 43.3, tokens 9480.9 to 5154.5.
  setup: Table 4, QwQ-32B-Preview + SimPO FCS+Reflection.
  quote: "AIME24 ... QwQ-32B-Preview 46.7 2.6 9480.9 38.4% 84.4% ... +SimPOFCS+Reflection 43.3 1.7 5154.5 39.8% 92.0%"
  where: p.10, Table 4. The paper text says "maintains model performance", but AIME24 drops 3.4 points.
- Claim: the shortest of 10 samples is more efficient than greedy decoding, which shows the model can produce efficient responses.
  number: greedy 3.1 solutions / 1434.8 tokens; shortest 2.5 / 1051.3; longest 4.1 / 2258.7.
  setup: Table 2, PRM12K training data, correct samples only.
  quote: "Greedy 3.1 1434.8 55.6% 72.6%"
  where: p.8
- Claim: the SFT, DPO, RPO and SimPO comparison on MATH500 (training on shortest response). SimPO shrinks tokens by 22.3%.
  number: SFT 93.2 / 2359.5; DPO 94.0 / 1929.5; RPO 91.6 / 2015.7; SimPO 92.4 / 1871.8. SimPO reduces tokens by 22.3%.
  setup: Table 4, MATH500.
  quote: "SimPO achieves the best results, reducing the number of generated tokens by 22.3% on MATH500."
  where: p.10

LIMITS
- Only math and science QA: ASDIV, GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA, AIME24. Nothing on code, agents, tool use or open-ended tasks.
- Models studied are QwQ-32B-Preview, DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-R1-Preview (appendix case). The mitigation is tested only on QwQ-32B-Preview, "because it is available for post-training". These are late-2024 models and may not describe current reasoning models.
- The fix is training (self-training with SimPO), not prompting. There are no prompt-level experiments, no "think less" instructions and no token budgets. The paper mentions token-budget prompting only as related work (Han et al. 2024).
- Solution splitting depends on Llama-3.3-70B, and strategy clustering depends on GPT-4o. No human validation is reported.
- The "efficiency" metrics count tokens after the first correct answer as waste. They give no credit for verification and can be gamed by short answers. The authors concede that FCS "decreases performance on the difficult MATH500 test set, which may require more rounds of reflection."
- The conclusion names future work: adaptive compute that adjusts to problem complexity, and better efficiency metrics.
- No limitations section; no variance or seeds reported; single runs.

BUILDS ON: self-training, STaR (Zelikman et al., 2022) and Ho et al. 2023; PRM12K (Lightman et al., 2024); SFT (Wei et al. 2022a); DPO (Rafailov et al. 2024); RPO (Pang et al. 2024; Liu et al. 2024); SimPO (Meng et al. 2024). The clustering prompt follows Ye et al. 2024. Related work: token-budget-aware reasoning (Han et al. 2024), Kimi k1.5 long-to-short (Kimi et al. 2025), Damani et al. 2024, Manvi et al. 2024, self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023b), chain-of-thought (Wei et al. 2022b; Kojima et al. 2022). Models: OpenAI o1 (OpenAI 2024), QwQ (Qwen 2024), DeepSeek-R1.

CODE: none in the paper. Metric definitions in text form (p.5-7), as extracted: "ξO = 1N N∑i=1 σi ˆTiTi" and "ξP = 1N N∑i=1 DiTi". The clustering prompt is in A.2, p.16-17: five criteria for what counts as a distinct solution, with output "cluster1 [solution names] reason for cluster".

FIGURES
- Fig. 1, p.1: (a) tokens on "2 plus 3?" for o1-like vs conventional models; (b) token-accuracy plot on MATH500. Fastest summary of the whole paper.
- Fig. 2, p.3: a 13-solution QwQ output for 2+3, with ξO = 4.3% and ξP = 35.8% as worked examples.
- Fig. 3, p.4: distribution of solution counts per test set.
- Fig. 4, p.4: solutions and tokens by MATH500 difficulty level.
- Fig. 5, p.5: index of the first correct solution.
- Fig. 6, p.6: distinctness ratio by solution index.
- Fig. 7, p.8: efficiency by difficulty level.
- Fig. 8, p.16: DeepSeek-R1-Preview on the same question (the extraction contains no figure text).
I did not run the figures script.

PROBLEMS: Figure text is duplicated and garbled in the extraction, so figure-derived numbers (especially Fig. 7) are uncertain. The pypdf page-level print was cut at 40k chars, and I re-extracted the rest. No embedded instructions found. Reference text was skimmed. The mismatch between "less than 50% outcome efficiency" at Level 1 and the Fig. 7 values (57.5%, 57.1%) is unresolved; verify in the PDF image before citing level-wise numbers.
